question.:question/problem: Evaluate $\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}[f(r(t))]$ at $t=1$ given that $∇f(x,y)=\left(8 x e^{x^{2} + y}\right)\,i+\left(4 e^{x^{2} + y}\right)\,j$ and $r(t)=\left(\sin{\left(t \right)}\right)\,i+\left(3 t + \cos^{2}{\left(t \right)}\right)\,j.$
question.:question/worked-solution:
The chain rule in vector form states that

$$
\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}[f(r(t))]=∇f(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t).
$$

In addition, we've been given that

$$
∇f(x,y)=\left(8 x e^{x^{2} + y}\right)\,i+\left(4 e^{x^{2} + y}\right)\,j.
$$

First, we substitute $x=\sin{\left(t \right)}$ and $y=3 t + \cos^{2}{\left(t \right)}$ into $∇f(x,y)$ to find $∇f(r(t)):$

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f(r(t)) & =\left(8 x e^{x^{2} + y}\right)\,i+\left(4 e^{x^{2} + y}\right)\,j\Big|_{x=\sin{\left(t \right)},\,y=3 t + \cos^{2}{\left(t \right)}} \\  & =\left(8 e e^{3 t} \sin{\left(t \right)}\right)\,i+\left(4 e e^{3 t}\right)\,j\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we calculate the derivative of $r(t),$ which is

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}\left(\sin{\left(t \right)}\right)\,i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}\left(3 t + \cos^{2}{\left(t \right)}\right)\,j \\  & =\left(\cos{\left(t \right)}\right)\,i+\left(- 2 \sin{\left(t \right)} \cos{\left(t \right)} + 3\right)\,j.\end{aligned}
$$

Applying the chain rule, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}[f(r(t))] & =∇f(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t) \\  & =\left(\left(8 e e^{3 t} \sin{\left(t \right)}\right)\,i+\left(4 e e^{3 t}\right)\,j\right)\cdot \left(\left(\cos{\left(t \right)}\right)\,i+\left(- 2 \sin{\left(t \right)} \cos{\left(t \right)} + 3\right)\,j\right) \\  & =\left(8 e e^{3 t} \sin{\left(t \right)}\right)\cdot \left(\cos{\left(t \right)}\right)+\left(4 e e^{3 t}\right)\cdot \left(- 2 \sin{\left(t \right)} \cos{\left(t \right)} + 3\right) \\  & =\left(8 e e^{3 t} \sin{\left(t \right)} \cos{\left(t \right)}\right)+\left(- 8 e e^{3 t} \sin{\left(t \right)} \cos{\left(t \right)} + 12 e e^{3 t}\right) \\  & =12 e e^{3 t}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, evaluating the above at $t=1,$ we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}[f(r(t))]\Big|_{t=1} & =12 e e^{3 t}\Big|_{t=1} \\  & =\left(4 e^{4} \sin{\left(2 \right)}\right)+\left(- 4 \left(-3 + \sin{\left(2 \right)}\right) e^{4}\right) \\  & =12 e^{4}.\end{aligned}
$$

\begin{aligned}∇f(r(t)) & =\left(\frac{1}{x}\right)\,i+\left(\frac{3}{y}\right)\,j\Big|_{x=4 t^{2} + 2,\,y=\operatorname{atan}{\left(4 t \right)}} \\  & =\left(\frac{1}{2 \left(2 t^{2} + 1\right)}\right)\,i+\left(\frac{3}{\operatorname{atan}{\left(4 t \right)}}\right)\,j\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we calculate the derivative of $r(t),$ which is

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}\left(4 t^{2} + 2\right)\,i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}\left(\operatorname{atan}{\left(4 t \right)}\right)\,j \\  & =\left(8 t\right)\,i+\left(\frac{4}{16 t^{2} + 1}\right)\,j.\end{aligned}
$$

Applying the chain rule, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}[f(r(t))] & =∇f(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t) \\  & =\left(\left(\frac{1}{2 \left(2 t^{2} + 1\right)}\right)\,i+\left(\frac{3}{\operatorname{atan}{\left(4 t \right)}}\right)\,j\right)\cdot \left(\left(8 t\right)\,i+\left(\frac{4}{16 t^{2} + 1}\right)\,j\right) \\  & =\left(\frac{1}{2 \left(2 t^{2} + 1\right)}\right)\cdot \left(8 t\right)+\left(\frac{3}{\operatorname{atan}{\left(4 t \right)}}\right)\cdot \left(\frac{4}{16 t^{2} + 1}\right) \\  & =\left(\frac{4 t}{2 t^{2} + 1}\right)+\left(\frac{12}{16 t^{2} \operatorname{atan}{\left(4 t \right)} + \operatorname{atan}{\left(4 t \right)}}\right) \\  & =\frac{4 \left(16 t^{3} \operatorname{atan}{\left(4 t \right)} + 6 t^{2} + t \operatorname{atan}{\left(4 t \right)} + 3\right)}{\left(2 t^{2} + 1\right) \left(16 t^{2} + 1\right) \operatorname{atan}{\left(4 t \right)}}.\end{aligned}
